existing.description: The Rufford Small Grants Programme funds fieldwork costs for small-scale, pilot nature conservation projects run by early-career conservationists in developing and emerging economy countries. Funding is staged across four levels - 1st Rufford Small Grant up to GBP 7,000, 2nd Rufford Small Grant up to GBP 8,000, Booster Grant up to GBP 12,000 and Completion Grant up to GBP 18,000 - and the Foundation aims to provide between 50% and 100% of project costs, requiring evidence of co-funding where it is not the only funder. Only fieldwork costs are considered, and award holders must provide project updates and a final report that are posted on their Rufford webpage. There are no deadlines, so the programme was open on the verification date.
eligibility: Applicants should be in the early stages of their conservation careers; priority is given to those undertaking an MSc or PhD (or equivalent) or who graduated from such studies in the past 3 years
We do not fund undergraduate students studying for a BSc or equivalent
Projects must have a nature conservation focus
Applicants must be working in an eligible country
We support small-scale or pilot projects
Ideally the Foundation should provide between 50 and 100% of the costs of the project; where The Rufford Foundation is not the only funder, evidence of co-funding is required
Only fieldwork costs will be considered

For species-focused projects, the species must not be listed as Least Concern at a global level in the IUCN Red List; species not on the list because they have not been assessed but thought to be globally threatened are also considered
Projects can focus on particular species, threatened habitats, or issues such as human-wildlife conflict or community education
existing.eligibility_summary: Early-career conservationists undertaking an MSc or PhD (or equivalent) or graduated from such studies in the past three years, working on a nature conservation project in an eligible country, on species not listed as Least Concern globally, with only fieldwork costs claimed; undergraduate students are not funded.
benefits: Staged funding pathway: 1st Rufford Small Grant, 2nd Rufford Small Grant, Booster Grant, Completion Grant
Project updates and a final report are published on the recipient's Rufford webpage
Access to a global network of Rufford grantees and conferences
coverage: Up to GBP 7,000 at 1st Rufford Small Grant stage
Up to GBP 8,000 at 2nd Rufford Small Grant stage
Up to GBP 12,000 at Booster Grant stage
Up to GBP 18,000 at Completion Grant stage
Ideally 50% to 100% of the total cost of the project
requirements: Be in the early stages of a conservation career (current MSc or PhD student, or graduated from such studies in the past 3 years)
Have a project with a nature conservation focus
Be working in an eligible country
Submit a small-scale or pilot project proposal
Provide evidence of co-funding where The Rufford Foundation is not the only funder
For species projects, show that the species is not globally Least Concern
Make only one funding application in any 12-month period
documents: Online application form via the Rufford Foundation application portal (an account is required to access the form)
Evidence of co-funding from other sources where The Rufford Foundation is not the only funder
Final report on project completion, copies of which are posted on the recipient's Rufford webpage
application_method: Learn about the grants available and the four funding levels
Check eligibility: early career stage, nature conservation focus, eligible country, threatened species or habitat
Create an account on the Rufford application portal
Complete the online application form and submit it
If funded, provide project updates and a final report on completion, copies of which are posted on your Rufford webpage
After at least 12 months from the date of payment and with updates and a final report provided, apply for the next funding stage
existing.selection_notes: The published criteria are the general criteria and general exclusions, project focus rules (including the IUCN Red List rule for species projects), the country eligibility list and the staged progression rules. The specific scoring method and decision process are not published on the pages read. Selection is effectively gated by the staged pathway: each further stage requires completion of the previous project, its updates and final report, and a minimum 12-month gap after payment, and for Booster and Completion Grants evidence of co-funding or sustainability planning.
existing.best_fit: Conservationists in the early stages of their careers - current MSc or PhD students, or people who graduated from such studies in the past three years - running a small or pilot nature conservation project on threatened species, habitats, human-wildlife conflict or community education in an eligible country, who can show a clear conservation benefit.
existing.notes: No deadlines - applications can be submitted at any time of year. Only fieldwork costs are funded. Undergraduate students are not funded. General exclusions: pure research with no obvious conservation benefit; expeditions where the applicant must raise funds to participate; attending conferences or seminars; publishing books. One application per 12-month period; a rejected applicant must wait 12 months before reapplying; a funded applicant cannot apply again for at least 12 months. On receipt of a Completion Grant you cannot apply for further Rufford funding.
existing.application_period: Rolling. Applications can be submitted at any time of year, with no published closing date. One application per 12-month period per applicant.
existing.deadline_display: There are no deadlines - applications can be submitted at any time of year. You can only make one funding application in any 12-month period; if an application is rejected you must wait 12 months before you can reapply; if you are funded you cannot apply for further support for at least 12 months.
